title: The Cave as womb and birth canal

beats.beat: Prisoners sit bound by feet and neck, watching shadows of wooden copies carried by puppeteers before a fire.
beats.reading: Ordinary life: we take matter, separateness, injustice and death as real. 'It seems, but it is not.'

beats.beat: One prisoner is suddenly and mysteriously released and turns around.
beats.reading: Conception and gestation: confusion, veils removed, while the light of consciousness is quietly fed.

beats.beat: The others mock him as mad.
beats.reading: The embryo must stay hidden, humble and quiet, eating only pure food on every level.

beats.beat: Near the exit he is dazzled and in pain.
beats.reading: The longest night of the soul: labour pains that are also death pains.

beats.beat: A helper drags him out by force.
beats.reading: Birth 'suddenly' with a midwife-teacher, into the place of the Good.

beats.beat: Outside he first sees by starlight and moonlight, reflections and shadows.
beats.reading: Truth is first lived emotionally, as experience without understanding, like a newborn.

beats.beat: He strengthens and finally looks at the Sun itself, understanding it caused everything in the cave.
beats.reading: Stabilised, the soul beholds the Sun of the Good, first principle and first cause.

beats.beat: He is sent back down into the cave.
beats.reading: Immanence: to awaken others. Below they said he died; above he was born; on return he seems risen from the dead.

title: The Cave: free hands and the turn back

beats.beat: Prisoners are chained by legs and neck, but not by the hands.
beats.reading: Hands are will, an extension of the heart: in love and will we stay free to move.

beats.beat: Behind the wall the wonder-workers (θαυματοποιοί) carry objects before a fire; each prisoner sits in their own little box discussing shadows.
beats.reading: Each stage is a mode of our own mind: conjectures, phobias, beliefs, ideologies to be deconstructed.

beats.beat: Release comes 'suddenly' and Plato calls it λύσις τε καὶ ἴασις.
beats.reading: The sudden may be a blow of fate or an inspiration; leaving is liberation and therapy.

beats.beat: Outside, he cannot look at the sun at once, like someone stepping from a dark basement into an Aegean summer, so he sees reflections in water first.
beats.reading: Ascent is gradual; at the summit even νόησις is transcended in the mystics' 'devouring fire'.

beats.beat: Those who have seen the sun are compelled to go back down.
beats.reading: Love and justice bring them back; initiation is complete only with immanence.

beats.beat: Prisoners deep in a dark, damp cave are chained at legs and neck and take shadows for reality.
beats.reading: Whoever has not escaped the futile mechanism of βίος lives in this cave.

beats.beat: Their hands are free.
beats.reading: Free will can never be subjugated; it is the key to changing one's state.

beats.beat: They sleep and do not remember.
beats.reading: The chains are λήθη; the cave is sleep in the cosmic dream, and the exit is awakening.

beats.beat: The Matrix retells the story.
beats.reading: Plato in futuristic form: today's shadows are social-media scrolling and phenomena themselves.

beats.beat: The child is born in a cave.
beats.reading: Plato's Cave: the state of consciousness of the body.

beats.beat: He is laid in a manger (φάτνη).
beats.reading: The region below the solar plexus where, in the Timaeus, the irrational powers live; awakening hatches between solar plexus and heart.

beats.beat: Two animals stand by the manger.
beats.reading: The spleen and the liver, the two organs of that region; also a pun on ἄλογα, horses and the irrational.

beats.beat: The Virgin conceives and Joseph doubts.
beats.reading: Despoina is the soul conceiving ineffably; Joseph is the mind that attacks the spiritual news, yet a sacred protection holds.

beats.beat: Herod sends soldiers to kill the infant.
beats.reading: Illusory forces threaten the newborn consciousness, which is still soft and vulnerable.

beats.beat: The family flees into Egypt.
beats.reading: The newborn must be kept hidden, quiet and humble; Egypt as 'gate of gates of light'.

beats.beat: On 21 December the sun seems to stand still.
beats.reading: The soul's deepest dive into the body, its winter solstice, the entry into the Cave.

beats.beat: On the 25th it begins to climb again: light is reborn.
beats.reading: Four days later, and four is Pythagorean establishment: what was performed in the depths is consolidated.

beats.beat: Antiquity celebrated the Dionysia and Heliougenna; later came Christmas.
beats.reading: All encode the same archetype: the birth of the sacred infant, the second birth of the soul.

beats.beat: In the mysteries of Samothrace the whole procession led to contact with 'the Child'.
beats.reading: The Child is Aion, the ever-being within us.

beats.beat: Heraclitus: Aion is a child playing draughts; the kingship is the child's.
beats.reading: The pieces are numbers and possibilities; at each moment the child manifests a new world, role or life.

beats.beat: The child is 'new and always ancient' (νέον, ἕνον).
beats.reading: The newborn is a revelation of what we always were, forgotten through Lethe.

beats.beat: Kore, daughter of Demeter, descends to Hades.
beats.reading: As bearer of death (φέρουσα φόνον) she lives the death of truth: identification with the body.

beats.beat: The light within her is activated.
beats.reading: As Φερσέφασσα, bearer of light, she sets out on the path of gestation and stripping.

beats.beat: She returns to her mother.
beats.reading: As Φερέπαφα, bearer of touch, she touches the immortal and returns to Demeter.

beats.beat: Leto flees.
beats.reading: She flees Lethe, forgetting.

beats.beat: She first gives birth to Artemis.
beats.reading: Artemis is ἀρετή: out of forgetting, first virtue.

beats.beat: Then Apollo is born on Delos.
beats.reading: Apollo is the divine light born on δῆλος, 'manifest': then truth becomes manifest.

beats.beat: Odysseus travels home from book Α to book Ν, the centre of the poem.
beats.reading: The return journey: transcendence, the soul reaching its Ithaca.

beats.beat: From Ν to Ω he must kill the suitors to secure Ithaca.
beats.reading: The suitors are habits, passions, programmes and old worldviews; killing them means bringing light to them and integrating them.

beats.beat: This takes longer than the voyage.
beats.reading: The immanent stage is the longest: traumas and karmic programming come up.

beats.beat: The eagle-mother pushes her chicks out of the nest so they fly.
beats.reading: Being and nature do not let awakened souls stay above; they are pushed back into becoming.

beats.beat: Plato says the freed will not be allowed to stay above.
beats.reading: Answers from her audience: to awaken others, to consolidate, to practise, to complete the cycle, to see all is one.

beats.beat: Alexander had beauty, strength, wealth and glory.
beats.reading: Everything at the level of γίγνεσθαι.

beats.beat: He said he owed ζῆν to his parents and εὖ ζῆν to his teacher Aristotle.
beats.reading: The good life comes through paideia, not possessions.

beats.beat: He said that if he lived again he would want to be Diogenes, who had nothing.
beats.reading: The man who had everything tells us it did not bring fullness.

beats.beat: Odysseus asks to be tied to the mast.
beats.reading: While fortune's wheel turns (εὐτυχία), eudaimonia is staying on one's central inner axis.

beats.beat: An ancient actor's mask sticks to his face and will not come off.
beats.reading: When the soul is too attached to roles and costumes it needs surgery.

beats.beat: Surgery is performed and the patient sleeps long to recover.
beats.reading: Depression can be that spiritual surgery, and its sleep a passage from the sleep of routine to waking.

beats.beat: The fighters of the 1821 revolution were 'drunk' on love of an ideal.
beats.reading: Eros for freedom itself, not for a person or body, shows eros is liberating; ἐλευθερία contains ἔρως (attributions to Kalvos and Kolokotronis uncertain).

title: Dionysus, the mirror and the Titans

beats.beat: The Titans set a mirror before the child Dionysus.
beats.reading: The mirror is the reflection-world of becoming; we mistake the image for reality.

beats.beat: They dismember him.
beats.reading: Daily life fragments attention (work, children, parents, taxes); each pull creates a role we lock into.

beats.beat: An audience member: remove the mirror and he would know his whole self again. She agrees.
beats.reading: The Titans, from τείνω, are our own tendencies toward the outside; turning inward restores wholeness.

beats.beat: Near death, his students ask what to arrange.
beats.reading: He asks only to be buried face down.

beats.beat: Why? 'Soon what is below will come up.'
beats.reading: Parmenides' reversal and the μεταστροφή: what seems to be is not, what seems not to be, is. She calls it 'crazy wisdom'.

beats.beat: Each of us is given a role, a costume and a name.
beats.reading: The actor (ἠθοποιός) makes an ethos by how he plays.

beats.beat: Theatres stood in all the Asclepieia.
beats.reading: Theatre heals through catharsis.

beats.beat: The spectator wakes to the spectacle.
beats.reading: The θέασις is recognising who plays all the roles: the vision of the Good.

beats.beat: There are the sun, the eye and visible things.
beats.reading: The eye is the most sun-like organ, a sleeping sun that stores sunlight and wakes when light touches it.

beats.beat: A fourth term hides: light, the 'third kind'.
beats.reading: Like Δ, triangle and number four: we never see light itself, only objects.

beats.beat: The sun gives growth and nourishment without being any of them.
beats.reading: The Good is self-luminous, the cause of knowledge but beyond it.

beats.beat: The analogy: the Good, the soul's eye (νοῦς), truths, and truth as light.
beats.reading: The soul is Good-like and carries a fiery sun; the Good's light is truth and its heat is eros.

title: Apollo and Dionysus shake hands at Delphi

beats.beat: At Delphi the two gods are shown together.
beats.reading: Not only Nietzsche's Apollonian and Dionysian, but the god-man: divine and human nature as one equation to solve in incarnate life.

title: The longest night and the holy infant

beats.beat: The longest night of 21 December, Christmas on the 25th, and the triple night of Heracles' conception (reconstructed, uncertain).
beats.reading: Absolute darkness, the 'dark night of the soul', comes before the final ascent and rebirth.

beats.beat: 'I am what has been, what is and what will be', written in a temple of Athena (cited via Proclus).
beats.reading: Athena is the wisdom of the cosmic fire, the immortal divine intellect; justice is that fire's self-regulation.

beats.beat: Hestia keeps the undying flame at the centre of Olympus.
beats.reading: Ἑστία is οὐσία: our essence is the primordial fire.

beats.beat: Odysseus is drenched by Poseidon's waves.
beats.reading: Passing through becoming, we 'got the flame wet' with passions.

beats.beat: The flame is still within.
beats.reading: Philosophy rekindles the inner Hestia.

beats.beat: Apollo is always depicted young.
beats.reading: He symbolises the One, the single pole; the One never ages or knows time, so unity is youth.

beats.beat: Two horses and a charioteer.
beats.reading: The horses are desire and the spirited part; the charioteer is reason below and nous above.

beats.beat: The chariot is a vehicle.
beats.reading: Her addition: fiery nous must 'cool' (ψύχεται) into soul to join the game of matter.

title: The Hyades and the dry soul

beats.beat: The Hyades in Taurus, near Orion, bring the rains.
beats.reading: Αὔη, dry, is ἀ- plus ὕω: the soul not rained upon, warmed dry by the fire of the Good.

title: The Cave and its forgotten return

beats.beat: Prisoners sit chained in a cave, taking shadows for reality.
beats.reading: The usual dualist reading: escape the cave of the senses and stay in the light of pure intellect.

beats.beat: One prisoner is freed, climbs out and knows the source of light.
beats.reading: Leaving the cave, remembering your nature and knowing pure consciousness is only half of the path.

beats.beat: Plato insists the freed must go back down, even against their will, and the city's founders must see to it.
beats.reading: The return is the part dualists forget, and it is the key to the whole allegory.

beats.beat: The returnee goes back with the soul's eye opened by the light.
beats.reading: Only now can the sensible world be truly understood, celebrated and raised to its highest beauty.

beats.beat: Those who stay below believe their satisfactions are real life.
beats.reading: 'Life in the cave' in the negative sense is believing that satisfying the senses brings eudaimonia.

title: The Allegory of the Cave (Republic VII, 514a)

beats.beat: Prisoners are chained at neck and legs deep in a cave, able to look only at the wall in front.
beats.reading: This is the human being before paideia, 'unhewn wood', with no all-round vision.

beats.beat: Behind them a fire burns, and along a low wall people carry statues and figures whose shadows fall on the wall, like a puppet or shadow theatre.
beats.reading: On the external level the puppeteers are media, propagandists and power centres; on the inner level they are our own mind, which loves good-guy and bad-guy scripts.

beats.beat: Glaucon finds the image strange; Socrates answers that the prisoners are 'like us'.
beats.reading: Our whole life, conversations and interests can be shadows and echoes.

beats.beat: A prisoner is freed, dragged resisting up the steep ascent; his eyes burn, and he sees first by starlight at night, then by day, then the sun itself.
beats.reading: The process of paideia is gradual and painful; the sun is the Good.

beats.beat: Looking back, he sees that the honours and 'degrees' given below for predicting shadows are worthless.
beats.reading: Status in the cave, including expertise about appearances, loses all value once the source is seen.

beats.beat: Out of compassion he goes back down; his eyes hurt in the dark and the others mock him and might even kill him.
beats.reading: The awakened are called back to serve; and he now sees that everything below had the same cause as above, the Good.

beats.beat: The allegory sits in the Republic, Plato's political work.
beats.reading: The path concerns our humanity as well as our divinity: no one should govern before awakening.

beats.beat: At the climax of the Symposium, Diotima, Socrates' teacher in eros, describes the final degree of eros, where one beholds a κάλλος ἀμήχανον.
beats.reading: ἀμήχανον means without 'mechanism', without form, mode or way.

beats.beat: Diotima cannot describe this beauty.
beats.reading: Not because she lacks words but because it is ineffable, unknowable, ungraspable.

beats.beat: She approaches it by negation: no body, no limbs, no colour, no size.
beats.reading: This is 'a wonderful non-dual description', the most language can do beyond the duality it is made for.

beats.beat: The lover beholds the beauty itself.
beats.reading: This beauty is what is beheld in awakening.

beats.beat: Plotinus, in 'On the Beautiful', borrows Odysseus' words: let us flee to the beloved fatherland.
beats.reading: Our fatherland is where we come from, where our Father is, and it is also our τέλος, eudaimonia.

beats.beat: Odysseus leaves Circe and Calypso despite their pleasures and beauty.
beats.reading: The soul must leave even pleasant attachments to go home.

beats.beat: The journey is not made on foot, by chariot or by ship.
beats.reading: Close the eyes and wake to another way of seeing that everyone has and few use.

beats.beat: Odysseus finally reaches Ithaca.
beats.reading: Her twist: he does not return to Ithaca, he wakes up in Ithaca, realising he was always there.

beats.beat: Odysseus reaches the Phaeacians, a civilisation with knowledge and technology far beyond Ithaca's.
beats.reading: Philosophy can become an advanced understanding or a mental sport.

beats.beat: He is offered Nausicaa and could stay.
beats.reading: Sophisticated understanding is attractive and can become a resting place.

beats.beat: He leaves anyway and goes home.
beats.reading: High understanding is a station, not the goal: it must become νόστος, return to the true self.

beats.beat: Odysseus had once been in Ithaca and left, then longed to return.
beats.reading: We too were 'there' in the One and left through the pull of the Other.

beats.beat: The goat Amalthea nourishes the baby Zeus.
beats.reading: Zeus is our νοῦς, our awareness; the myth is a symbol of our own being.

beats.beat: Capricorn, the 'goat-horn', is where the winter solstice falls.
beats.reading: The horn is the soul-food released at this gate; when the nous is fed rightly it remembers itself.

beats.beat: The horn of Amalthea is the horn of plenty.
beats.reading: At the end of the descent, the Plutonian power transformed in the depths becomes your own horn of Amalthea.

beats.beat: The Titans tear Dionysus apart.
beats.reading: The Titans, from τείνω, are the tensions of becoming that polarise us and pull us off centre.

beats.beat: Only the heart is left.
beats.reading: The tensions of becoming eat away at us until only the centre remains.

beats.beat: Athena saves the heart, and Dionysus is reborn.
beats.reading: Wisdom saves the centre so we can be reborn.

beats.beat: Dionysus holds Delphi for the three winter months while Apollo is with the Hyperboreans.
beats.reading: The year itself alternates two natures.

beats.beat: Apollo returns at the spring equinox.
beats.reading: The return of light at the balance point of the year.

beats.beat: A vase shows the two gods shaking hands before a palm tree.
beats.reading: The union of the two natures, which she maps onto the Same (Apollonian) and the Other (Dionysian).

title: The birth of Heracles at the triple night

beats.beat: Zeus lies with Alcmene for three nights (the τριέσπερος).
beats.reading: The three days the sun appears to 'stand' after the solstice, 22 to 24 December.

beats.beat: Heracles is conceived and born.
beats.reading: The inner hero is thrice sown, gestated and born.

beats.beat: 25 December follows: Ἡλιούγεννα, the birth of the sun.
beats.reading: The birth of the inner sun; she reads Alcmene as ἀλκή + μήνη, the moon with strength.

beats.beat: After the Eleusinian equinox Persephone goes down to Pluto.
beats.reading: Darkness means introversion: you descend into the subconscious to heal yourself.

beats.beat: In the underworld she meets Pluto's realm.
beats.reading: Face your monsters and hidden passions and trace their roots in events, family and ancestors.

beats.beat: Demeter's seeds are sown.
beats.reading: Pull out the weeds and sow virtue, love, kindness, cooperation and truth.

beats.beat: In their Orphic hymn the Hours come with many colours and many scents.
beats.reading: Colour and scent are the sensible doors through which the ascent happens.

beats.beat: They lead Persephone back up to the light in a spiral ascent.
beats.reading: The Horai are the moment of the soul's awakening, born when we see sensible and intelligible as one continuum.

beats.beat: The other gods of Olympus travel between worlds and come back.
beats.reading: These are the soul's changing movements, the Circle of the Other.

beats.beat: Hestia alone never leaves the centre.
beats.reading: She is the Circle of the Same in the soul, the still motion that keeps us in our essence.

title: The soul plunged into the river (Timaeus)

beats.beat: The soul's orbits, wrapped in body and elements, are sunk as if into a great river.
beats.reading: A 'first baptism': immersion in the manifestation of God called the river of the elements.

beats.beat: The surging waves flow in and out through the soul's circles and buffet them.
beats.reading: This is the origin of sensation and of the newborn's confusion.

beats.beat: Odysseus crosses Poseidon's waves toward Ithaca.
beats.reading: She suggests this may describe the same voyage of the embodied soul.

beats.beat: Infant souls move randomly forward, back, right, left, up and down.
beats.reading: Proclus says this is not literally six directions but our sixfold experience in embodiment.

beats.beat: The Same and the Other get twisted, so the world appears upside down.
beats.reading: We take what changes for what is fixed: matter as stable, and the soul as doubtful.

beats.beat: As the inflow calms, the soul's motions recover.
beats.reading: Judgment of same and different becomes correct and the person is 'on the road to φρόνησις'.

beats.beat: Eternity (Aion) is a child playing draughts or dice, and the kingship is the child's.
beats.reading: Life is a divine game; being like that child is a good sign.

beats.beat: Einstein said God does not play dice.
beats.reading: For Heraclitus the cosmic child does throw dice: the probabilities and possibilities of the One.

beats.beat: The dice are thrown on the board of the world.
beats.reading: In the Aromatic talk she adds that sensation helps turn these possibilities into actuality.

beats.beat: Socrates says he is no teacher but a midwife, like his mother Phaenarete.
beats.reading: All souls are pregnant with the true self.

beats.beat: He calls on Artemis to help you give birth to what you carry.
beats.reading: The highest pregnancy is of the true self, the 'birth of light'.

title: The little house on the prairie

beats.beat: You settle down happily in your little house.
beats.reading: The need for stability: the Circle of the Same.

beats.beat: Then something itches: a chicken coop, a vineyard, boredom, a new adventure.
beats.reading: The need for change: the Circle of the Other. Both are in all of us.

beats.beat: Some heroes have a divine father and a mortal mother.
beats.reading: Following Proclus: they perfected the Circle of the Same.

beats.beat: Others, like Achilles, have a divine mother and a mortal father.
beats.reading: They perfected the Circle of the Other, which she suggests is harder because it includes the seven centres (her own interpretation).

beats.beat: The ring gives power without limits.
beats.reading: Too much power or money, misused, flings you far from your centre: a hedonistic 'summer solstice'.

beats.beat: Excess cannot last.
beats.reading: The scale will swing back, so moderate circumstances are a blessing.

beats.beat: In Hesiod everything emerges from Chaos.
beats.reading: Chaos is not evil, dark or non-existent; it is simply not a 'something', the boundless.

beats.beat: Kazantzakis spoke of the Abyss.
beats.reading: Both are approximations of the formless One, not identities: she does not equate the One with Chaos.

beats.beat: Diogenes walks around naked, urinates in the agora and hits people with his staff.
beats.reading: Awakened sages do not fit a respectable template.

beats.beat: Plato the aristocrat, Socrates the family man, hermits and illiterate shepherds were also sages.
beats.reading: History offers wildly different sages so that we cannot dogmatise awakening.

beats.beat: Her grandmother from Asia Minor still put tangerine peel on the electric hob at 85.
beats.reading: A small household rite of scent.

beats.beat: Her mother, grandmother and great-grandmother in Smyrna burned peel on the embers in winter, with no flowers or chemical perfumes.
beats.reading: Smell carries memory across generations.

beats.beat: Theseus escapes the labyrinth by Ariadne's thread.
beats.reading: Even in the cave of ignorance we can take the thread and leave the labyrinth of conditions, which are never perfect.

beats.beat: Someone can drive you to the rock at Sounion.
beats.reading: Knowledge takes you to the edge.

beats.beat: Diotima speaks of the plunge into the open sea.
beats.reading: You must let go of knowledge and dive into lived union.

beats.beat: Apollo's temple bears 'Know thyself'.
beats.reading: The god is not asking us to study our separate personalities.

beats.beat: The command is in the singular and may be read 'know it'.
beats.reading: Apollo calls consciousness to turn its eye on itself and know itself as the one Self.

beats.beat: At the entrance to Apollo's temple stand Know thyself, the cryptic E and Nothing in excess; Plutarch wrote a whole treatise on the E.
beats.reading: Know thyself and the E are Apollo's own words; the others belong to the Seven Sages.

beats.beat: Pilgrims arrive hoping to meet the god.
beats.reading: Instead of a welcome, Apollo poses a riddle: to know me, know yourself.

beats.beat: Beside the precept stands the E, read as εἶ, you are.
beats.reading: You already are the divinity you seek; it is not outside in the temple or in things.

beats.beat: Both messages greet every visitor.
beats.reading: Together they point to the science of the self, where the secret of happiness lies.

title: The birth and name of Pythagoras

beats.beat: His mother Parthenis and father Mnesarchus go to Delphi to ask about Mnesarchus's merchant trips in the East.
beats.reading: Parthenis means the virgin, pure, virtuous one; the setting is already sacred.

beats.beat: The priests ignore the trade question and prophesy about the unborn son: he will surpass all in wisdom and beauty and benefit humanity. Parthenis is renamed Pythais.
beats.reading: The child's mission is marked as divine before birth.

beats.beat: He is named Pythagoras: Πυθ- for the Pythia and Pythian Apollo, plus ἀγορά, the marketplace.
beats.reading: The agora of goods and ideas is ruled by Hermes, lord of logos.

beats.beat: Iamblichus says this was not merely because the Pythia announced him.
beats.reading: He was an emanation of Apollo entering the agora of the many, the realm of becoming, to bring enlightened teaching.

beats.beat: Pythagoras's father finds a foundling in the woods, called the star child, who seems to feed on droplets of sun and water from the air and is raised with Pythagoras.
beats.reading: She tells it as one of the myths or true stories of his divine origin, something like a pranic diet.

title: The education and travels of Pythagoras

beats.beat: Taught early by Thales and Anaximander, he is recognised by the Seven Sages, who give him letters for the Pharaoh.
beats.reading: He is welcomed by the wisest of his time.

beats.beat: Egypt's priests test and accept the foreigner; he studies there 22 years.
beats.reading: Egypt's esoteric schools were the Harvard or Oxford of spiritual consciousness.

beats.beat: Then 12 years in Persia with the Magi, and by some accounts India and the Brahmins; he leaves Greece at about 17 and returns at about 56.
beats.reading: A lifetime of initiation across traditions (her figures).

beats.beat: Back in Greece he studies with Orphic mystics, meets Epimenides the purifier in Crete, is initiated into the Mysteries and serves a year at Delphi as high priest.
beats.reading: Energetic cleansing, pranic nourishment and karma are in the Hellenic scriptures, not only Eastern or New Age.

beats.beat: He keeps long silences, glows with an aura, recalls past lives, and founds his school at Croton since Samos was not fertile ground.
beats.reading: The founder of philosophy was a realised contemplative.

beats.beat: In the Republic, intellectual truth is the light.
beats.reading: Knowledge illuminates, but it is not the source.

beats.beat: The Good, or the One, is the Sun, the source of reason and mind.
beats.reading: The end of knowledge is to move beyond knowledge into its source.

beats.beat: At four she already wondered about death; at about 14 she meets Plato in a school textbook and asks her teacher for more.
beats.reading: The questions of who I am and why I am here come early.

beats.beat: Reading the dialogues by the fireplace one winter, she loses all sense of time and space in an immersion of light.
beats.reading: Perhaps a form of samādhi: absence, wholeness, fulfilment.

beats.beat: She returns activated, knowing this is why she was born.
beats.reading: Philosophy began for her as a lived experience, not an academic subject.

beats.beat: Apollo, the god from afar, stands for the always-transcendent One.
beats.reading: Non-duality, the source that never enters form.

beats.beat: Dionysus is the god incarnate, leading festivals and plays.
beats.reading: He plays in duality, and his theatre shows the roles we play in life.

beats.beat: The two gods shake hands.
beats.reading: Duality and non-duality are one, so the Greeks built no monasteries and even Pythagoras returned to marry and teach politicians.

beats.beat: The prisoner turns from the shadows and leaves the cave.
beats.reading: The transcendent step: the mystic closes eyes and ears and turns inward.

beats.beat: The freed one must go back down into the cave.
beats.reading: Seeing that the cave is of the same essence as the world of Ideas: immanence.

beats.beat: The levels of the cave, from shadows up to the light.
beats.reading: A map of consciousness from impressions and feeling tones to concepts and awareness.

beats.beat: In the Timaeus the priests tell Solon that the Greeks are always children because they forget their history.
beats.reading: Greek civilisation is far older than Greeks remember.

beats.beat: An earlier Greek civilisation fought the Atlanteans when their technology threatened the world, and survived in pockets; Proclus elaborates.
beats.reading: The tradition runs deep, so Orpheus (around 1700 or even 3000 BC) can begin its modern phase as an avatar and son of the Muses.

beats.beat: Zeus leads the gods and is always chasing a goddess or a mortal woman to father more children.
beats.reading: Zeus is creative mind, consciousness in its creative operation.

beats.beat: Goddesses and mortal women bear his children.
beats.reading: They are the divine ideas and the ordinary ideas that consciousness mingles with.

beats.beat: Every union produces a birth.
beats.reading: Every birth is a world: all we experience is a child of consciousness.

beats.beat: Zeus has two names, Δίας and Ζεύς.
beats.reading: Δίας divides and projects, Ζεύς unifies and returns things to the source: the two movements of creative mind.

title: Odysseus: from the two to the One

beats.beat: Odysseus wanders far from home and finally returns to Ithaca.
beats.reading: In an esoteric etymology, his name traces a path from the two (duality) to the Good (εὖ) to the One (ἕν).

beats.beat: The return is a kind of death and rebirth.
beats.reading: A mystagogic death of the belief that I am only the local self; nobody actually dies.

beats.beat: Hestia holds a light at a single point.
beats.reading: The infinite localises in one place to have a human perspective.

beats.beat: A wheat seed carries a programme and grows when conditions allow.
beats.reading: Humans carry the telos of eudaimonia and bring the inner fountain into life as creativity.

beats.beat: Homer shows Apollo angry and Hera quarrelling with Zeus.
beats.reading: Homer codes cosmic and karmic laws in analogies: Apollo's anger is the reaction our actions bring back.

beats.beat: Plato removes such stories from children's education.
beats.reading: The divine has no jealous or warring states, and children who take them literally justify their own anger.

title: Diotima and the plague of Athens

beats.beat: Diotima, a priestess and shaman from Arcadia, comes to Athens during the plague.
beats.reading: She cleanses the energetic, karmic residue of the polis.

beats.beat: She becomes Socrates' teacher.
beats.reading: She initiates him into oneness and love as the path to awakening.

beats.beat: During the campaign Socrates stands all night in meditation.
beats.reading: Proof he was a contemplative, not a dry rationalist.

beats.beat: At dawn he salutes the sun, then goes to fight for Athens.
beats.reading: Realisation and civic duty go together.

beats.beat: Poseidon is usually linked with the trident and storms at sea.
beats.reading: He is the higher octave of love, the cohesive force of the universe.

beats.beat: He rules the waters.
beats.reading: The waters are the cosmic ocean, the energetic soup of modern cosmology.

beats.beat: He holds the trident, shaped like Ψ.
beats.reading: The Ψ is that of ψυχή: souls travelling in the ocean that unites all.

beats.beat: At Agathon's house, Socrates recounts what Diotima taught him about eros.
beats.reading: The only surviving text where we see a woman teaching, Plato quoting her as if she were present.

beats.beat: Eros starts with attraction to one person.
beats.reading: Only the first of seven levels.

beats.beat: Eros climbs to love of values, institutions and laws.
beats.reading: Political eros: good laws habituate us toward eudaimonia.

beats.beat: Eros opens finally to the whole universe.
beats.reading: The soul's rush to recognise that we are one with all.

title: The teacher and the code of ethics

beats.beat: A disciple asks a teacher for the code of ethics: how to behave toward others.
beats.reading: The question assumes separate selves.

beats.beat: The teacher answers that there are no others.
beats.reading: If the self is common, ethics follows naturally: see all as your own self.

beats.beat: The host recalls the Golden Rule.
beats.reading: The Greeks go further than refraining from harm: love and help the other as a mother helps her children.

beats.beat: Diotima instructs her young pupil Socrates about eros.
beats.reading: A teaching so ahead of its time that it meets modern needs.

beats.beat: She tells him which education he must follow as budding philosopher and Athenian citizen.
beats.reading: An erotic pedagogy, the education humans are called to in every age.

beats.beat: That education teaches how to practise love in life.
beats.reading: Love is a teachable discipline at the heart of civic education.

beats.beat: Its fruit is virtue.
beats.reading: Through virtue, the longed-for eudaimonia.

title: The bookshop and the Autobiography of a Yogi

beats.beat: At about 23 or 24, waiting for a boat on a summer island pilgrimage, she browses the Classics shelf of a seaside bookshop.
beats.reading: She was already a young girl reading ancient writers.

beats.beat: A young visitor brings her an old edition of Yogananda's Autobiography of a Yogi; she refuses, and he says she will miss the boat unless she buys it.
beats.reading: It was not even him in that moment: something spoke through him.

beats.beat: She surrenders and buys it; two days of reading turn her life upside down and she meditates alone on an isolated beach.
beats.reading: Deconstruction (Derrida, Foucault) gave her no path; she needed a living, structured path in the present.

title: The Oxford seminar on Plato's mathematics

beats.beat: A speaker presents Plato's view of mathematics as an initiation into the divine.
beats.reading: The texts themselves describe a practice.

beats.beat: She asks how to apply it, and colleagues reply that they are students of the philosophers, not philosophers.
beats.reading: It mirrors church practice in Greece: you may read about Christ but not become one.

beats.beat: She recalls Jesus saying you will do what I did and more, and Plato's call to walk the path.
beats.reading: Both teachers asked for practice, not commentary.

beats.beat: In Dharamsala she meets special beings; one asks why she is up in the Himalayas.
beats.reading: The question turns her search around.

beats.beat: Everything you are looking for is where you started from.
beats.reading: A message of spirit and heart valid for all Westerners, not only Greeks.

title: The Odyssey as the soul's journey

beats.beat: Odysseus leaves Ithaca with the Greek army under Agamemnon for Troy.
beats.reading: The soul descends into human nature: war, competition, passions, greed, the daily struggle for survival.

beats.beat: He wanders and suffers for years.
beats.reading: Ὀδύσσομαι, I suffer: the sense of lack and of losing one's centre.

beats.beat: The goddess Athena guides him.
beats.reading: Divine guidance: philosophy, ethics and knowledge, healing the passions.

beats.beat: He returns to Ithaca.
beats.reading: The νόστος to the inner centre: fullness, freedom, eudaimonia.

beats.beat: Aeschylus, Sophocles and Euripides could not invent plots and characters; they retold existing archetypes, mostly Homeric.
beats.reading: Each had to light the sacred, universal myths in a new way.

beats.beat: Audiences imitated the heroes' passions (μίμησις) and identified with them.
beats.reading: Only true symbols can bring κάθαρσις, which proves these stories are archetypes.

title: Why the hymn to Ares comes last

beats.beat: Hymn 84 is to Hestia: the hearth, essence, falls asleep into the world of the many.
beats.reading: Essence (οὐσία) enters the 'divine sleep' of incarnation.

beats.beat: Hymns 85 and 86 are to Sleep and Dream.
beats.reading: Life is God's dream; our name and story are projections on the cave wall.

beats.beat: Hymn 87 is to Death.
beats.reading: Death ends the dream and begins the return home: a transition, not an end.

beats.beat: Hymn 88, the last, is to Ares the Warrior.
beats.reading: Ares rules Aries, the first sign, at the spring equinox: the end joins the beginning, so we must be warriors through death and into the next birth.

beats.beat: A seed's shoot cracks the soil with its head so spring can 'open' the ground.
beats.reading: The forcing power of birth is sacred, not brutal: this is Ares.

beats.beat: The ram charges head-on with its horns, as Ares wears a great helmet.
beats.reading: The ram of Aries is the same upward, head-first impulse.

beats.beat: The embryo pushes out into the world.
beats.reading: We are born 'into the contest' of life, hence γενέθλια, birthday.

beats.beat: In the Iliad Athena wounds Ares and he is carried to Olympus.
beats.reading: Wisdom outranks force: someone had to stop Ares, and only Athena could.

beats.beat: He complains to Zeus that Zeus favours Athena (?).
beats.reading: Force resents wisdom's precedence, but Zeus has him healed: force is restored to its place, not destroyed.

title: Ares follows Aphrodite to the Trojans

beats.beat: Lured by love, Ares abandons the Achaeans' protection and switches sides.
beats.reading: Our vital force must not be dragged by passion and desire.

beats.beat: Athena puts him back in his place.
beats.reading: Force must serve higher mind and providence; the outer shell of Olympus is the most exposed layer.

title: Ares and Aphrodite, parents of Harmonia and Eros

beats.beat: Ares and Aphrodite unite.
beats.reading: She calls this Greek sacred union (ἱερογαμία), what other traditions call tantra.

beats.beat: They give birth to Harmonia and Eros.
beats.reading: Ares works among opposites; raised, he becomes a harmoniser, but he needs Aphrodite's love, beauty and purity to learn to unite.

title: Tea and scones for Mrs Medusa

beats.beat: She jokes about politely offering Medusa or the Hydra tea, scones and biscuits.
beats.reading: A monster or tyrant does not understand courtesy, only force, the power of life.

beats.beat: Instead one brings out Ares and Athena's 'dreadful' spirit.
beats.reading: Not shouting or hitting: it is the energy you carry, so even your peace 'has roots'.

title: The Greek Revolution and the Constitution

beats.beat: Greek freedom was won with arms, not with discussion.
beats.reading: Ares and Athena cooperated: law-founding force is illegal for the old order and legal for the new.

beats.beat: The constitution passed because some had fought the liberation struggle, and the force stayed to guard it.
beats.reading: Will, deliberation and force give birth to a state, outer and inner.

beats.beat: Prisoners are chained deep underground in one hollow of the cave.
beats.reading: Humanity before spiritual παιδεία, identified with the body in a 'material, objective' world.

beats.beat: Their legs are bound.
beats.reading: No movement means no freedom, and for the ancients movement is life: they do not truly live.

beats.beat: Their necks are bound.
beats.reading: The link between heart and mind is blocked (she adds: the throat chakra); they cannot find or express their truth.

beats.beat: Their hands are left free.
beats.reading: Free will, προαίρεσις, which nobody can ever bind and which will free them.

beats.beat: Figures carried before a fire cast shadows the prisoners argue over.
beats.reading: Screens, news, governments and internet; beyond that the whole visible world; beyond that the brain's inner cinema lit by the synapses' 'fire'.

beats.beat: Some rise, wander, meet a freed person who returned to help, and are pulled out.
beats.reading: An ineffable, spontaneous act of the unmoved will, then help from one who has seen through identification with the body.

beats.beat: Their eyes burn, then they see birds, trees and finally the sun.
beats.reading: A gradual process ending in vision of the One, the Good, pure divine nature.

beats.beat: The cave's mouth (στόμιον) leads out.
beats.reading: It is not a place in space-time; banging on the wall takes you deeper. The exit is a turning inward: you are the gate.

beats.beat: The cave and the outside world seem far apart.
beats.reading: The cave is the Good's 'underground': they differ in depth or vibration, so no GPS can route you between them.

beats.beat: Below, in the shadow theatre, they play coronaviruses, festivals, joys and sorrows.
beats.reading: The phenomenal world is a shadow play.

beats.beat: The one who has opened the curtain keeps watching.
beats.reading: Watching while remembering 'I am not this; I am this too, but more'.

title: The Cave as womb and tomb

beats.beat: Prisoners, chained from birth by neck and feet, see shadows cast by wonder-workers holding wooden objects before a fire.
beats.reading: Sleep and ignorance, full identification with the body: each of us is the shadow of himself. ('The Matrix took it from Plato.')

beats.beat: Suddenly some are freed and wander the cave, sensing another world.
beats.reading: Becoming: apprenticeship and pregnancy; they know they are soul but still identify it with the body.

beats.beat: Freed ones come down to help them out; the light dazzles them like lights switched on in a dark room.
beats.reading: They adapt by night and starlight before looking at the sun.

beats.beat: They see the sun of the Good.
beats.reading: The sun is pure Being.

beats.beat: From inside, the one who left seems to have 'died'.
beats.reading: As we say a loved one 'left': leaving the cave is death and second birth.

beats.beat: He must go back down.
beats.reading: No fairy-tale ending: he returns to recognise the One in every form.

beats.beat: Xanthippe laments and is sent away.
beats.reading: In her retelling Socrates says that if people knew how good it is afterwards everyone would leave, which is why they do not know.

beats.beat: Socrates goes calmly to his death.
beats.reading: Like an Olympic athlete stepping out on the day of the Games to perform what he trained for all his life.

beats.beat: The tragedians say only Helen's εἴδωλον, a 'hologram', was at Troy while she was in Egypt.
beats.reading: The war was fought over a shadow, like the cave's shadows.

beats.beat: Seferis writes of 'an empty tunic, a Helen'.
beats.reading: We fight and suffer for images we take as real.

title: Persephone, sought by mother and husband

beats.beat: Persephone descends to Hades and rises again.
beats.reading: The soul of each of us descends and ascends.

beats.beat: She is sought now by her mother, now by her husband Hades.
beats.reading: Mother is womb, Hades is tomb: the same pairing as the cave.

beats.beat: The coming festivals celebrate a sacred birth.
beats.reading: The soul conceives a sacred seed and begins to gestate.

beats.beat: Dionysus is devoured or dismembered by the Titans and vanishes.
beats.reading: The death of the separate self.

beats.beat: His heart was kept (?) and he was reborn.
beats.reading: The freed one who returns: rebirth beyond birth and death.

title: Socrates is told to make music

beats.beat: In the Phaedo Socrates' inner daimon tells him 'make music'.
beats.reading: Not 'learn the lyre': tune the soul's frequencies into harmony, which is virtue.

beats.beat: The harmony opens a gate.
beats.reading: Inner harmony is a gate to the cosmic ocean, the One.

beats.beat: The command continues: 'and work'.
beats.reading: Come back and embody the realisation as a way of life and as service.

beats.beat: Mnesarchus asks the Pythia about a trading trip to Syria.
beats.reading: An ordinary question, as we all ask.

beats.beat: Unasked, Apollo says the trip will go well and that Parthenis, pregnant without knowing it, carries a being who will surpass all in beauty and wisdom.
beats.reading: The first sign of Pythagoras' tie to Apollo; one meaning of his name is 'announced by the Pythian'.

beats.beat: Iamblichus places him in Apollo's retinue.
beats.reading: Sent 'like an avatar'; some even see him as Pythian Apollo in the marketplace of becoming.

beats.beat: Before incarnating, souls live in swarms serving central powers, the deities.
beats.reading: Deities are codes for archetypal cosmic energies.

beats.beat: No soul lives alone.
beats.reading: The universe is a polity: the many that are one together.

title: Astraeus, the boy who drank dew

beats.beat: Mnesarchus finds a boy of about ten on Samos, in a white chiton, gazing at the sky and drinking dew from the ether.
beats.reading: A being from the astral plane, 'fed on light'.

beats.beat: His name is Astraeus, and he becomes the young Pythagoras' companion.
beats.reading: Guardian and first teacher of a soul with a special mission (her account, from Iamblichus).

beats.beat: Abaris comes from the Hyperboreans flying on Apollo's arrow.
beats.reading: A teacher 'from another dimension'.

beats.beat: His name is read as ἀ-βάρος, 'without weight'.
beats.reading: Lightness as a mark of the realised being.

beats.beat: Polycrates recommends the young Pythagoras to Pharaoh Amasis.
beats.reading: In her telling, the start of long study abroad.

beats.beat: He passes from the priests of Memphis to Heliopolis to Diospolis.
beats.reading: She calls the Egyptian mysteries 'the Harvard of spirituality'.

beats.beat: The last priests set impossible trials (hunger, thirst, hardship) to be rid of the Greek.
beats.reading: He passed every one with excellence and won their admiration.

beats.beat: Zeus's first daughters are the Horai.
beats.reading: Beauty: ὡραῖον read as 'the omega that flows', the flowing whole.

beats.beat: Then come the Moirai.
beats.reading: The whole divides into shares (μοῖρα), and each part feels separate.

beats.beat: Last come the Charites.
beats.reading: Through divine grace you return to unity, or the form ends and returns to the whole anyway.

beats.beat: Apollo kills the serpent Python to found Delphi.
beats.reading: Python from πύθω, to rot: the power that dissolves what is dead, rotten and false in us.

beats.beat: His father is Mnesarchus, a merchant and gem-engraver.
beats.reading: Memory (μνήμη) ruling (ἄρχω): the masculine principle, mind, cleansed so that it remembers its primordial nature.

beats.beat: His mother is Parthenis, the virgin, later renamed Pythaïs.
beats.reading: The feminine principle, the heart, purified.

beats.beat: From the two, Pythagoras is born.
beats.reading: When mind and heart are both purified, the 'Pythagoras within' is born: the light that knows universal laws and shares them in the agora.

beats.beat: Heaven, Ouranos, is married to Earth, Gaia.
beats.reading: The heavenly and the earthly, absolute and relative, are not two; we are ephemeral in one view and eternal in essence.

beats.beat: Like many, she took a bag and went to India, studied Indian, Buddhist and Taoist texts, and went up into the Himalayas.
beats.reading: The search outside one's own culture.

beats.beat: A nameless teacher initiated her with the message: go back, you already have the whole tradition where it began.
beats.reading: The Greek tradition of awakening was there all along, and so it proved.

title: Newton on the shoulders of giants

beats.beat: Newton said he stood on the shoulders of giants.
beats.reading: She says he meant chiefly Aristotle, whom he copied in Greek in notebooks she has seen in England.

beats.beat: Greeks still mourn a difficult past.
beats.reading: Look at the heritage as Newton did: a base to build on, not nostalgia.

title: Athena born from the head of Zeus

beats.beat: Athena springs from the head of Zeus.
beats.reading: Zeus is νοῦς, the mind that divides and analyses or synthesises and joins.

beats.beat: She is the goddess of wisdom.
beats.reading: Wisdom is the τέλος and fruiting (κάρπισμα) of mind, which gratitude both invites and expresses.

title: The touch of the Three Graces

beats.beat: 'With Athena, move your hand too.'
beats.reading: Our own effort is necessary.

beats.beat: The Χάριτες touch a life.
beats.reading: Grace, synchronicity or the right conjuncture also completes eudaimonia; thanksgiving activates it.

beats.beat: Greece was offered safety if it let the aggressor pass and looked after only itself.
beats.reading: The temptation of ἰδιώτευσις: your little house, family and country will be fine; the others will suffer.

beats.beat: Greeks said «No».
beats.reading: A «No» to private interest: they identified with humanity and the whole earth, the 'light' inscribed in their name.

beats.beat: They faced death.
beats.reading: Defying death, they dis-identified from the ego and touched immortality as a state of consciousness; they were Hellenes in actuality.

beats.beat: Later generations did not plant the «Yes».
beats.reading: A «No» without a «Yes» is lame: no rooted foundations of παιδεία followed.

beats.beat: Heracles stands at the fork between Virtue (Ἀρετή) and Vice (Κακία).
beats.reading: The same dilemma faces each of us at every moment.

beats.beat: He must choose one road.
beats.reading: Each yes and no sets our steps; their resultant sets our course and whether life makes us blessed (μακάριοι).

beats.beat: Stormy seas toss Odysseus away from Ithaca.
beats.reading: The passions toss us on emotional seas and we lose our Ithaca.

beats.beat: Ἰθάκη rearranged gives ἠθική.
beats.reading: Coming home is ethics: regulating the soul toward virtue, which brings eudaimonia.

beats.beat: A strong seed is thrown into soil.
beats.reading: The «No» is the seed.

beats.beat: One connects with Demeter, goddess of agriculture, to tend, water and prune.
beats.reading: The «Yes» is this cultivation, which lets the «No» sprout, flower and bear fruit.

beats.beat: A she-dragon, the Python, occupies the oracle at Delphi and rots in the mud (πύθω, to rot).
beats.reading: The old, stagnant chthonic forces that occupy the sacred space of our soul: 'we are the oracle of Delphi'.

beats.beat: Apollo shoots her with a hundred arrows (ἑκατηβελέτης).
beats.reading: Why a hundred? It is the letter ρ, which stands for flow: stagnant waters must move, unstick and be cleansed.

beats.beat: The oracle is freed for the god of light.
beats.reading: Healing begins with the intention and will to change; nothing moves while we stay stuck.

title: Persephone and the descent into sleep

beats.beat: Persephone descends into Hades.
beats.reading: The soul descends into this world, 'and Hades is here': the world of sleep.

beats.beat: In the Kabeiric and Eleusinian mysteries the initiates pass through death or sleep and return.
beats.reading: Awakening is resurrection (ἀνάστασις): we 'move neighbourhood' to a place of light.

beats.beat: Prisoners sit chained, watching shadows.
beats.reading: Ordinary sleep: we take what we are told as real.

beats.beat: Some grow restless, try to break their chains and ask whether things are really as they are told.
beats.reading: Pythios, the first step: inquiry and an appetite for truth, while old forces still occupy us.

beats.beat: Plato speaks of the 'release and healing' (λύσις καὶ ἴασις) of the chains.
beats.reading: Apollo the healer, ἀπολούων: washing away what we thought we knew.

beats.beat: One leaves the cave for the light.
beats.reading: Ismenios, those who have knowledge, who begin the mystical education.

beats.beat: The freed one goes back down to those still inside.
beats.reading: ὁμοπολῶν: returning to the many to make music, the political step of consciousness.

title: Odysseus and the day of return

beats.beat: Odysseus leaves Ithaca for the war told in the Iliad.
beats.reading: The soul goes out into the war of the many: the Neoplatonic procession.

beats.beat: He fights and wanders for years, longing for the νόστιμον ἦμαρ, the day of return.
beats.reading: We too have fought long and long for our home, which is eudaimonia.

beats.beat: He comes home to Ithaca.
beats.reading: The return to the source, matching procession, remaining and return.

beats.beat: Patients purified themselves for days before entering the sanctuary.
beats.reading: Medicine is holistic: illness starts in nous, then soul, then body, so healing starts by purifying the soul.

beats.beat: In incubation (ἐγκοίμησις) the patient saw Asclepius in sleep.
beats.reading: What they saw was the inner Asclepius.

beats.beat: The god gave the command to heal.
beats.reading: The soul itself gave the command: light and pure vision heal.

beats.beat: Leto labours on Delos before Apollo is born.
beats.reading: Birth pangs (ὠδῖνες) are the first signs of a birth: Delios is the beginning of manifestation, through signs and synchronicities.

beats.beat: An audience member asks why Apollo never took Zeus' place.
beats.reading: There is no Apollo without Zeus, the demiurgic nous that keeps generating ideas and natures, hence his many children.

beats.beat: Apollo moves through creation.
beats.reading: He comes to remind us not to get lost in phenomena but to return to the essence Zeus generates.

beats.beat: Asked how Zeus could be 'born', she answers.
beats.reading: Talk of time is a convention for the human mind: these are simultaneous, qualitative differentiations, not history.

beats.beat: Socrates' daimonion told him only one thing: μουσικὴν ποίει καὶ ἐργάζου, make music and work at it.
beats.reading: Not 'become a kithara player' but learn to harmonise opposites: reach the last Apollonian step.

beats.beat: Socrates walks the agora and is condemned by pseudo-politicians who love money and power.
beats.reading: He lived the political step of consciousness that the music passage opens.

title: Apollo and Dionysus as two states of one universe

beats.beat: In On the E at Delphi, Plutarch treats Apollo and Dionysus as one.
beats.reading: Two states of the universe, not two rival gods.

beats.beat: Dionysus is the dyadic mind.
beats.reading: The one becoming many.

beats.beat: Apollo is the universe's fulfilment, when it 'catches fire' to return into unity.
beats.reading: The many returning to the One in a luminous, non-material fire, comparable to the Stoic ἐκπύρωσις.

beats.beat: An audience member raises Nietzsche's Birth of Tragedy.
beats.reading: He 'began from good premises', but Plutarch already saw the two as one.

beats.beat: Greek tradition knows a heavenly Aphrodite, Οὐρανία.
beats.reading: Eros 'from here upward', with pure emotion and through the spirit.

beats.beat: It also knows a common Aphrodite, Πάνδημος.
beats.reading: Eros approached in a lustful, bodily way; societies promote one kind or the other and could be studied that way.

title: Kingdoms built and lost in one night

beats.beat: In history and in myth, whole kingdoms are built in the name of eros and destroyed in a single night in its name.
beats.reading: Proof that eros is the strongest power in the universe and a double-edged knife. She names no example.

title: Diotima teaches Socrates the erotic path

beats.beat: Socrates, the wisest of men, had a woman teacher, Diotima.
beats.reading: She stresses that the teacher of the wisest man was a woman.

beats.beat: Diotima teaches him that self-knowledge, philosophy and awakening form an erotic journey.
beats.reading: Socrates calls it an erotic pedagogy; for her it is the central path of Greek philosophy.

beats.beat: She tells him the goal of eros coincides with the goal of human life.
beats.reading: Eros exists to remind us of the εὖ δαίμων we already are.

title: The Cave as a map of the mind (Open Microphone, 2023)

beats.beat: Plato tells the cave as an image of people who have never left a cave or seen the sun.
beats.reading: Humans understand stories better than concepts, so he gives the Sun and Line again as a picture; the cave is his answer to what paideia is.

beats.beat: The prisoners are bound by the neck and cannot turn their heads.
beats.reading: They see only one direction, one-sidedness, the opposite of Athena's owl, which turns its head and sees the whole from above.

beats.beat: On the wall they see shadows of wooden figures that wonder-workers carry before a fire.
beats.reading: The shadows are εἰκασία: the personality's shadows, traumas and projections. The figures are the sensible objects about which we form opinions and convictions, the deep cave.

beats.beat: The prisoners take the shadows for reality.
beats.reading: Double ignorance: they do not know that they do not know, and they call anyone who speaks of the spiritual mad.

beats.beat: Suddenly the chains break and one prisoner turns round.
beats.reading: Plato says only ἐξαίφνης; she reads the trigger as a crisis or as the soul's ripe hour, the same moment others call grace.

beats.beat: The others call him back to keep commenting on the wall.
beats.reading: This first transitional stage is the hardest: he no longer believes what he knew and has not yet tasted what comes after.

beats.beat: He meets the wonder-workers.
beats.reading: Outwardly they are the makers of mass reality, but in truth the one wonder-worker is the nous itself.

beats.beat: He comes out, dazzled, and must relearn everything; first the stars and moon, later the sun.
beats.reading: The night sky is the astral plane, the sun the spiritual plane; he enters ideas and numbers, and must culminate in μέθεξις with the sun of the Good.

beats.beat: Outside are the true plants, animals and things of which the figures were images.
beats.reading: Today we are the idol-worshippers (the host's phrase): we take the image the mind gives an essence for reality, as modern physics also shows.

beats.beat: The freed one goes back down into the cave.
beats.reading: As a psychopomp like Hermes, and because the apprenticeship is incomplete until one descends into becoming; there he sees cave and Good are one and darkness is dimmed light.

title: The Sun simile: the source that is not light

beats.beat: Socrates asks which sense most resembles light; the answer is sight, the most sun-like.
beats.reading: Sight lets Plato make the ascent from the visible to the intelligible, from sunlight to the light of consciousness.

beats.beat: Eye, objects and sun form a triangle, but sight needs a third kind: light.
beats.reading: Light is the condition: turn off the lights and we see nothing.

beats.beat: The sun's light reaches the eye and activates the power of sight already in it.
beats.reading: The model of education: do not stuff children with knowledge; activate the source within, because knowledge is recollection.

beats.beat: The sun is the source of sight, light and visibility, yet is none of them.
beats.reading: So the Good is the source of truth and knowledge without being either: a spring is not water.

beats.beat: Raised to the intelligible, the Good is the sun, the nous the eye, ideas and numbers the objects, and truth the light.
beats.reading: Awakening is not knowing the One but uniting with the unknown; whoever insists on knowing it is stuck a stage before.

title: Piraeus, justice and three symbolic names

beats.beat: Socrates goes down to a festival in Piraeus, and the sons of his friend Cephalus begin a discussion on what is just.
beats.reading: Hence the subtitle 'On the Just': justice, the virtue of virtues and the state of awakening, is the theme of the whole Republic.

beats.beat: Socrates proposes to take Glaucon and Adeimantus and found a new polity.
beats.reading: The names are not random: Socrates the inner one (reconstructed), Glaucon the brightness of the soul, Adeimantus the adamantine steadfastness needed to build the polity.

beats.beat: When asked to define paideia, Socrates says he will speak in a parable.
beats.reading: The cave is a real answer to a real question, not a figure of speech to pass the time.

title: Pythagoras's three decades in the East

beats.beat: Pythagoras studies in Greece with Presocratics, including Thales of Miletus.
beats.reading: He first gains the Presocratics' science.

beats.beat: At 16 he leaves Greece for the strongest esoteric temples and schools of Egypt, as Plato later would.
beats.reading: Over three decades of paideia in the 'centres of light', Egypt and later Babylon, which guarded a universal knowledge (Egypt having it from Atlantis, if we believe Plato; reconstructed).

beats.beat: He returns at about 56 and founds a new system, naming the path 'philosophy'.
beats.reading: He weds Presocratic science to universal mystagogy; so racial identity must not be imposed on spirituality, or it becomes another cave.

title: Marcus Aurelius rules an empire without being Caesarified

beats.beat: Marcus writes notes to himself, not for publication, while at war (the host adds this context).
beats.reading: He uses them to keep himself in the presence of truth amid court, courtiers and soldiers.

beats.beat: He warns himself: do not be Caesarified.
beats.reading: Do not identify so much with the role you play.

beats.beat: He tells himself that everyone around him, of every race, family and class, is his sibling.
beats.reading: We are all children of the same nous, so dividing people by origin is a bodily illusion.

title: Hermes the psychopomp brings Persephone back

beats.beat: Those freed from the cave go back in to help the others.
beats.reading: This leads to the epithet ψυχοπομπός, guide of souls.

beats.beat: Hermes, holding the caduceus, leads Persephone back to her mother Demeter, with the spring.
beats.reading: Hermes is the symbol of the teacher who unites the two worlds.

title: The Horai, daughters of Zeus and Themis

beats.beat: The Horai are the first daughters of Zeus by his second wife Themis, goddess of justice.
beats.reading: The soul's ripe hour belongs to cosmic justice: when all conditions are met, it opens like chamomile in spring.

beats.beat: Their sisters are the Graces (Χάριτες).
beats.reading: What she calls the hour, others call grace, divine grace; it is the ἐξαίφνης in which the prisoner comes out.

title: Justinian's decree and the knowledge underground

beats.beat: The new religion wants a monopoly on access to the divine.
beats.reading: A path to union with divinity through philosophy and science has to be cut: keep logic, ethics and pedagogy, bury the theology.

beats.beat: In the 6th century Justinian's decree forbids teaching mathematics, the mysteries and theology.
beats.reading: The knowledge goes underground, and from it come the alchemists and later orders.

beats.beat: Positivism and the Enlightenment continue along the same line.
beats.reading: Philosophy becomes a Frankenstein, taught without its mystagogy.

beats.beat: Seventeen centuries later, it can be brought back without danger to life.
beats.reading: Ours is the first generation free to reunite philosophy's spiritual aspects with its science.

title: The professors and the myth of Er

beats.beat: At university, she was taught that Plato 'got tired' and threw in the myth of Er about metempsychosis at the end of the Republic.
beats.reading: A symptom of philosophy stripped of its mystagogy: what scholars cannot understand, they call a mistake, because it threatens the ego of the knower.

beats.beat: Odysseus calls himself Οὖτις, Nobody.
beats.reading: Pure consciousness is not someone but the nobody who is all, the One; whoever still says 'I am the awakened one' has not arrived.
